findings.message: Saved pins are only rewritten after a rename inside `confirmChat`, and only in the confirming viewer's own conversations. Two variants still go stale. (1) `tag_release` or an environment rename run over MCP, by an agent or by a pipeline. MCP is the main channel, and nothing there calls `repinConversations`. (2) Other people's saved conversations that hold pins keyed on project key and version or on project key and name. All pins made before 057 are keyed that way, including the old `get_release` / `get_release_history` row pins. Those pins then read null, or read a different release once the old version tag is reused. Fix: make the read tools resolve old pins by id. For example, rewrite stored key-based pins to ids lazily when they are next read, or record the rename and look it up at read time. Then drop the repin step that only works for the actor in chat.
findings.scenario: Maya has a saved conversation pinned to get_release_history {projectKey:'CON', version:'v2.4.0'}. An agent calls tag_release v2.4.0→v2.4.1 over MCP, then creates a new release v2.4.0. Maya reopens the conversation from History, and the pin resolves to the new, unrelated v2.4.0 release.

findings.message: Release, environment and deployment pins are now keyed on ids so that a rename can't strand them. The new proposal pins (board card, and the release page's proposal list via `get_proposal`) are keyed on `key`, which can also change: the specclaw sync rekeys hand-made proposals (`ProposalRekeyed`). Nothing repins on a rekey. Fix: key proposal pins on the proposal id. Add an optional `proposalId` to `get_proposal`, so that a key given with it only narrows the result, the same rule used for releases.
findings.scenario: Pin the hand-made card CON-1001. Sync rekeys it to CON-017. The pin {key:'CON-1001'} now reads null, or reads another proposal if that key is later reused.

findings.message: `repinConversations` runs after `confirmAction` has committed the write, inside the same try. If the repin throws (a DB error or a timeout), the catch returns `outcomeOf(e)`. The card then shows an error or open state for a write that actually happened, the response carries no `moved`, and the page doesn't follow the re-tag. Fix: run the repin in its own try/catch after the write and still return `state: 'done'` with `moved`. Log the repin failure, or report it as a separate warning in the note.
findings.scenario: Confirm tag_release CON v2.4.0→v2.4.1 and have the chat.conversation update fail. The card shows the failure and the user retries. The release is already v2.4.1, so the retry fails with 'not found'. The page stays on /CON/v2.4.0, which renders 'Release not found'.

findings.message: The docstring at line 203 says one rule covers releases, environments and deployments: with an id, any key part that is also given only narrows the result. `getEnvironment` only narrows on `projectKey`. When `environmentId` is given, `name` is ignored, so this copy of the rule disagrees with `releaseWhere`/`isRelease`. Fix: also require `x.name === ref.name` when both are given, or derive all three readers from one shared helper.
findings.scenario: get_environment {environmentId:<CON UAT id>, name:'Prod'} returns the UAT environment. The equivalent get_release {releaseId:<v2.3.0 id>, version:'v9'} returns null.

findings.message: Release-page pins are keyed on ids, so `repinAll` never matches them (`match` needs projectKey/version in args), and their labels are never updated. After a confirmed re-tag, the open conversation's pins still read 'CON v2.4.0 proposals' and 'CON v2.4.0 on Prod, …' while the record is now v2.4.1. Consider a repin that matches on `releaseId` and only relabels.
findings.scenario: Re-tag v2.4.0→v2.4.1 from the release page. The chat drawer's pin chip still says 'CON v2.4.0'.

findings.message: The scripted rules match versions and environments with `(\S+)`, and opportunity numbers with `PS-\d{4}`. The Ask amax prompts can carry versions with spaces (the delivery test re-tags to '2.3.1 rc/1'), environment names with spaces, and PS numbers of up to 6 digits (`NUMBER`). Those prompts fall through to list_projects in e2e and local demos.
findings.scenario: 'Record a deployment of CON 2.3.1 rc/1 to Pre Prod' → no tool call.

findings.message: After a confirmed rename, the client replaces its whole pin state with the conversation's saved pins (`setPins(o.pins)`). Pins are saved only when a turn is sent. Any pin added or removed in the drawer since the last turn is lost, or a removed one comes back, on every repinning confirm. Fix: send the `repin` to the client and apply repinAll to the current client pins, rather than overwriting them with the server copy.
findings.scenario: Send a turn with the release pinned, which proposes tag_release. Pin proposal CON-017 without sending. Click 'Add it' on the tag card → o.pins is the saved [release pin], so CON-017 disappears from the composer and the next message goes without it.

findings.message: The repin covers only one path: a rename confirmed through chat, and only the conversations of the person who confirmed it. Two variants are missed. tag_release or upsertEnvironment(rename) called directly over MCP (agents, pipelines) returns `repin` but nothing applies it. Other people's saved conversations keep projectKey/version or projectKey/name pins that now resolve to null; the test even asserts that the other user's pin stays stale. Fix: resolve by id instead. Make the rename service rewrite every matching saved pin, tenant-wide, in the same transaction as the write (chat.conversation is chat's own schema, so do it through a chat command, not from the delivery module). Or migrate old version- and name-keyed pins to releaseId/environmentId once, so no pin depends on a renamable key.
findings.scenario: Sahan has a saved conversation pinned to get_release_history {projectKey:'CON', version:'v2.4.0'}. Maya re-tags the release to v2.4.1 via chat, or a CI agent does it via MCP tag_release. Sahan reopens the conversation from History → the pin resolves to null, so the release reads as not found.
